style_method: Ten women's category pages (T-Shirts, Shirts & Blouses, Sweaters & Cardigans, Jeans, Pants, Dresses, Jackets & Coats, Shorts, Skirts, Sweatshirts) paged with the page parameter until a page added no own-label style. Own label = product address starting BDG, UO, Out From Under, Kimchi Blue, Silence + Noise or Urban Renewal, which gave 688 distinct styles; outside brands excluded. Composition read from the Content + Care block in each product page, one page at a time. Lead fibre = highest share in the first composition listed (lining ignored); recycled polyester counted as polyester, rayon as viscose, spandex as elastane.
sample_basis: 78 of 688 own-label styles, stratified in proportion to category size (even spacing within each category). The site states about 4,557 items across the ten categories, outside brands included, so 688 is a floor: pages stopped early and own-label detection is by name. An advent calendar and a pyjama set were dropped. All 78 sampled pages stated a composition.
fab_basis: Of 78: cotton leads 44 (56.4%); synthetic leads 28 (35.9%: polyester 24, acrylic 2, nylon 2); viscose/rayon 5 (6.4%); linen 1 (1.3%); wool 0 as a lead (wool appears as a minor fibre in 2); cashmere 0; silk 0. Denim read as denim cloth: 7 of 78 (9.0%), 6 jeans plus a denim short. Cotton carries BDG, tees, pants, skirts; polyester carries dresses (11 of 16) and sweaters.
tech_named_fabrics: NONE (no named technical or branded fabric in the 78 sampled pages; no TENCEL, Lycra or similar named)
owned_facility: NONE found (the 10-K extract does not mention owned factories; it says UO uses agents and third-party manufacturers and about 4,000 vendors)
made_in_stated_share: 1 of 78 (1.3%): one dress says Made in the USA; the other 77 say "Imported"
heritage_claim: dated and placed: first store opened 1970 across from the University of Pennsylvania, West Philadelphia, by Dick Hayne, Scott Belair and Judy Wicks (URBN history page); nothing on where clothes are made
process_documented: no (the product pages and URBN brand page cover style and community, not making)
craft_reasoning: UO designs and buys from about 4,000 third-party vendors; no owned factory, mill or maker is named on any of the 78 sampled pages, 77 of which say only "Imported". One page says Made in the USA. The only dated, placed claim is the 1970 West Philadelphia first store, which is retail history. Nothing checkable about making, so a 1.
note: Part 1 dials read 22-23 Oct 2026 from urbanoutfitters.com US. Own label only: BDG, UO, Out From Under, Kimchi Blue (sample covers these four). UO sells many outside brands in every category; they are excluded and the site category totals include them. UO also sells men's: women's category pages only. Unisex pieces not identified. Sleepwear and swim excluded (one pyjama set and an advent calendar dropped). Two-piece sets (4 in sample) counted as one style. Status partial: 688 is a floor, and own-label detection is by product name.
